Step 6 closes a loop opened right back at signoff. The design was timed against corner models; measuring real corner silicon says whether those models were pessimistic, accurate, or—the dangerous case—optimistic.

Watch out for

  • Corner models optimistic against real silicon. The design was signed off against those models, and a gap here means the margin does not exist.
  • Split lots not actually at the corners. Material that drifted back toward center proves nothing about the edges.
  • Cpk not computed. Capability against the specification is what predicts production yield, and a pass/fail result does not.
  • Corner characterization skipped for schedule. The population's edges are then only seen in production, as an unexplained yield tail.
  • Process window recommendation not fed back to the fab. The data exists and the process keeps running at its original center point.

Why it exists

Hold the production readiness review—the cross-functional gate where every function states whether it is ready—and stand up change control for everything that follows.

This is the program's last formal decision point. After it, the product is in production and every change goes through customer notification. The review's value is that it forces each function to say ready or not ready on the record, which is a different act from being asked in a meeting whether there are any concerns.

Step 4's conditional items are where a review either works or becomes theatre. A conditional pass with an owner, a date and a consequence is a real mechanism; a conditional pass without them is an unconditional pass with a note attached.

Watch out for

  • Review held without evidence. Function-by-function assurances are not the same as qualification data, and a review that accepts them is not a gate.
  • Conditional items without owners or dates. The condition is then never closed and the pass was unconditional in practice.
  • Change control not established. Post-production changes then reach customers without notification, which is a contractual failure.
  • Dissent not recorded. A function that said not-ready and was overruled is the program's most valuable record if something goes wrong.
  • Document baseline not frozen. Which datasheet, which errata, which test program was released becomes ambiguous immediately.

Takes12ww10–w22 of the stage

Why it exists

Commit the supply chain and the ramp—wafers, substrates, HBM, assembly and test capacity—against a demand forecast, with the lead times and second sources that make the commitment real.

A ramp is a chain of commitments made months before the volume they serve. Substrates have long lead times, HBM is allocated across the industry, and assembly capacity is booked. Any one of them short stops the ramp, and none of them can be fixed quickly.

What it delivers

Step 8 runs last but covers everything before it. Each commitment made in steps 2 and 4 is a single point of failure, and the plan has to say what happens if any one of them fails—before it does.

Watch out for

  • HBM allocation insufficient. It is allocated across the industry and a shortfall stops the ramp regardless of everything else.
  • Substrate lead time underestimated. Advanced substrates are long-lead and capacity-constrained, and the buffer has to reflect that.
  • Ramp planned against an optimistic yield. Volume commitments then require more wafer starts than were booked.
  • No second source anywhere in the chain. Every single-source node is a single point of failure for the whole product.
  • Capacity committed before the readiness review. A conditional readiness outcome then meets an unconditional supply commitment.

Appendix A

GlossaryTERMS

Every abbreviation used anywhere in this document, expanded, with what it is and why a program manager would care. 184 entries. Each activity page lists the terms it uses.

Program and commercial 19

ASP
Average Selling PriceWhat the part is expected to sell for. With yield and cost it decides whether the program has a margin.
BOM
Bill of MaterialsThe itemized list of what goes into the product. An IP BOM lists every IP block the die needs and where it comes from.
BSP
Board Support PackageThe minimum software that lets a host boot and talk to the board. Its boundary with the firmware team has to be agreed, not assumed.
CI
Continuous IntegrationAutomated build-and-test on every change. In hardware it usually means nightly regressions rather than per-commit.
DOE
Design Of ExperimentsA structured set of experimental splits chosen so each variable's effect can be separated. How process windows get characterized.
FTE
Full-Time EquivalentOne person working full time. Derived here as M/M ÷ TAT in months — the team size implied while the activity runs.
KPI
Key Performance IndicatorA measurable target derived from a requirement. A requirement without a KPI cannot be tested at the end.
M/M
Man-MonthOne person working for one month. The unit of effort in this template; summing it across a stage gives the headcount the stage consumes.
NDA
Non-Disclosure AgreementThe contract that has to exist before a foundry, IP vendor or customer will share anything useful. Routinely on the critical path early.
NRE
Non-Recurring EngineeringOne-off cost — masks, tooling, IP licences — as opposed to per-unit cost. Dominates the business case for an advanced node.
PCN
Product Change NotificationThe formal notice to customers that something about a shipping product has changed. Once in production, changes go through it.
PO
Purchase OrderThe binding commitment to buy. Long-lead items (masks, substrates, HBM) need one far earlier than intuition suggests.
PPA
Power, Performance, AreaThe three quantities every chip design trades against each other. A "PPA target" is the contract the architecture must meet.
PRD
Product Requirements DocumentThe baselined statement of what the product must do. Everything downstream is an answer to it.
RFI
Request For InformationAn early, non-binding enquiry to a supplier — used to scope options before quoting.
RFQ
Request For QuotationA formal request for price and terms. Precedes a purchase order.
SW/FW
Software / FirmwareOut of scope for this template, which covers design and silicon enablement only — but the handoff boundary still has to be agreed.
TAT
Turn-Around TimeElapsed calendar time an activity occupies, in weeks. Not the same as effort — a 20-week activity may take one person or ten.
WIP
Work In ProgressMaterial already started but not finished. In a fab it is weeks of committed capacity that cannot be redirected.

Process, foundry and manufacturing 25

BEOL
Back End Of LineThe metal interconnect layers built above the transistors. Taped out about a month after FEOL to buy design-fix time.
CMP
Chemical Mechanical PlanarizationThe polishing step that keeps each layer flat. Drives metal-density fill rules in layout.
CPI
Chip-Package InteractionMechanical stress where die and package meet, driven by their different thermal expansion. The main reliability risk in 2.5D construction.
CoWoS
Chip-on-Wafer-on-SubstrateA 2.5D packaging technology: die placed on a silicon interposer, which sits on the substrate. The construction assumed here.
DK
Design KitUsed interchangeably with PDK; sometimes the assembly or package equivalent supplied by the OSAT.
DRM
Design Rule ManualThe foundry document defining what geometry is legal. Its version has to match the DRC deck actually being run.
DTCO
Design-Technology Co-OptimizationTuning design style and process options together rather than treating the process as fixed. Where standard-cell track height gets decided.
EUV
Extreme Ultraviolet lithographyThe lithography used at advanced nodes. Its layer count drives mask cost and cycle time.
FEOL
Front End Of LineThe transistor-forming steps of wafer fabrication. Taped out first in a split MTO, because it has the longest cycle time.
HD
High DensityA standard-cell flavor optimized for area rather than speed; HPC is its high-performance counterpart. Process option menus offer both.
KGD
Known Good DieA die screened at wafer sort as worth packaging. On a 2.5D part an escaped bad die costs an entire assembled module.
MDP
Mask Data PreparationTurning the design database into mask-writer input — fracturing, OPC, job deck. Weeks of work between tapeout and first wafer.
MPW
Multi-Project WaferA shared mask set carrying several designs. The cheap way to get a test chip fabricated.
MTO
Mask Tape-OutThe release of the design database to mask making. The irreversible commitment — masks cost millions and take weeks.
MTV
Mechanical Test VehicleA test vehicle for warpage, stress and assembly mechanics rather than electrical behavior.
OPC
Optical Proximity CorrectionPre-distorting mask shapes so the printed result matches intent. Part of mask data prep, after tapeout.
OSAT
Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and TestThe subcontractor that packages and tests the die. Owns the assembly process knowledge the program depends on.
PCM
Process Control MonitorThe test structures WAT measures. Their readings are the earliest signal that a lot drifted.
PDK
Process Design KitThe foundry's package of models, rules and libraries that makes a process usable. Its version and maturity gate everything downstream.
RDL
Redistribution LayerFine wiring on the die or interposer surface that moves connections to where the bumps are.
TSV
Through-Silicon ViaA vertical connection through a die or interposer. What makes stacked and 2.5D construction possible.
TTV
Thermal Test VehicleA test vehicle carrying heaters and sensors, used to characterize the package thermal path before real silicon exists.
TV
Test VehicleA structure built purely to learn about a process, not to sell. Retires risk before the real product commits.
ULK
Ultra Low-K dielectricThe fragile low-capacitance insulator in BEOL. Mechanically weak, which is why chip-package interaction stress matters.
WAT
Wafer Acceptance TestParametric measurement on scribe-line structures. Tells you whether the process was in spec independently of whether the chip works.

IP and libraries 13

AMS
Analog / Mixed-SignalCircuitry that is not purely digital. Characterized by simulation rather than by static timing, and on a different schedule from the digital flow.
HV
High VoltageDevices rated above the core supply — used in IO and power management.
IP
Intellectual Property blockA pre-designed functional block — a PHY, a memory compiler, a controller — bought or reused rather than written.
LDO
Low-Dropout regulatorAn on-die linear regulator giving a quiet local supply to sensitive analog blocks.
NoC
Network on ChipThe on-die interconnect fabric carrying traffic between blocks.
OTP
One-Time Programmable memoryFuse-based memory written once after manufacture — used for trim values, keys and repair settings.
PHY
Physical layerThe analog and mixed-signal circuitry that drives an interface's wires — as opposed to the digital controller above it.
PLL
Phase-Locked LoopThe circuit that multiplies a reference clock up to the operating frequency. Its lock range bounds the shmoo.
RF
Radio FrequencyHigh-frequency analog circuitry.
ROM
Read-Only MemoryFixed on-die memory, typically holding boot code.
SRAM
Static Random-Access MemoryOn-die memory. Usually generated by a compiler; when the compiler misses the PPA target, a custom instance has to be developed.
SerDes
Serialiser / DeserialiserThe circuit that turns parallel data into a high-speed serial stream and back. The heart of every high-speed interface.
VCO
Voltage-Controlled OscillatorThe tunable oscillator inside a PLL.

Design and implementation 34

AOCV
Advanced On-Chip VariationDepth- and distance-dependent OCV derating — less pessimistic than a flat margin.
CDC
Clock Domain CrossingA signal passing between unrelated clocks. Unsynchronized crossings fail intermittently and are invisible to simulation.
CPM
Chip Power ModelA compact model of the die's current demand, handed to package and board teams so they can size the PDN.
CPS
Chip Power/Signal modelCPM extended with signal behavior, for combined power and signal co-analysis.
CTS
Clock Tree SynthesisBuilding the buffer network that delivers the clock. Sets skew, and consumes a large share of dynamic power.
DC
Direct currentZero frequency. A regulator specified only at DC says nothing about how it behaves where the digital load actually switches.
DFM
Design For ManufacturabilityChanges that improve yield without changing function — via doubling, spacing, fill.
DRC
Design Rule CheckVerifying that layout geometry obeys the foundry rules. A tapeout gate.
DVFS
Dynamic Voltage and Frequency ScalingChanging supply and clock at runtime to trade power against performance.
ECO
Engineering Change OrderA late, targeted change to a design that is otherwise frozen. A metal-only ECO touches routing layers alone.
EM
ElectromigrationMetal atoms drifting under sustained current, eventually opening a wire. Bounds how much current a given wire width may carry. In “3D EM” it means electromagnetic instead — field solving for package and board models.
FFN
Final Full NetlistThe netlist released for the last physical-design turn — RTL frozen, ECOs closed, no functional change beyond it.
GLS
Gate-Level SimulationSimulating the actual netlist with real delays. Slow, but catches what RTL simulation and STA both miss.
IO
Input / OutputThe circuitry and pads connecting the die to the outside world.
IPC
Instructions Per CycleHow much work the design retires per clock. Performance is frequency × IPC, so a max frequency target only means something alongside the IPC assumption behind it.
IR
IR dropSupply voltage lost across the resistance of the power grid (I × R). Too much and the logic misses timing that STA said was fine.
LEC
Logical Equivalence CheckingProving two netlists implement the same function — used after every synthesis or ECO step.
LVS
Layout Versus SchematicVerifying that the layout implements the intended netlist. The other tapeout gate.
MCMM
Multi-Corner Multi-ModeThe same thing as MMMC; vendors differ on word order.
MMMC
Multi-Mode Multi-CornerAnalyzing every operating mode against every process/voltage/temperature corner at once. The standard implementation setup.
N0/N1/N2
Netlist drop 0 / 1 / 2The successive netlist releases from synthesis to physical design. N0 is flow-flush — structurally representative but functionally incomplete — and each drop raises quality.
OCV
On-Chip VariationAllowance for variation between devices on the same die. AOCV and POCV are its advanced and parametric refinements.
PDN
Power Delivery NetworkEverything carrying current from the regulator to the transistors — board, package and on-die grid together.
POCV
Parametric On-Chip VariationStatistical OCV using per-cell sigma rather than a derate table.
PVT
Process, Voltage, TemperatureThe three axes of operating variation a design must survive. "Corners" are their extremes.
QoR
Quality of ResultsThe bundle of timing, area, power and congestion numbers a tool run produces. What "the netlist got better" actually means.
RDC
Reset Domain CrossingThe same hazard for signals passing between independently reset regions.
RTL
Register Transfer LevelThe synthesisable hardware description — Verilog or SystemVerilog. "RTL freeze" means no further functional change.
SDC
Synopsys Design ConstraintsThe file describing clocks, exceptions and IO timing. Wrong constraints make timing closure meaningless in both directions.
SSN
Simultaneous Switching NoiseSupply disturbance when many outputs switch together. Couples into interfaces as jitter.
SSO
Simultaneous Switching OutputMany outputs switching at once; the current step they draw is what produces SSN.
STA
Static Timing AnalysisExhaustive timing checking without simulation. The basis of timing signoff.
UPF
Unified Power FormatThe machine-readable description of power domains, isolation and retention. Carries power intent through the whole flow.
VDD
Supply voltageThe positive rail powering a block. "VDD collapse" is a deliberate momentary droop used as an SRAM write assist.

Verification and DFT 21

ATPG
Automatic Test Pattern GenerationComputing the input patterns that expose manufacturing defects, and the coverage they reach.
BIRA
Built-In Redundancy AnalysisOn-die logic that works out which spare rows or columns would repair a failing memory.
BISR
Built-In Self-RepairApplying that repair automatically. Turns memory defects from scrap into yield.
BIST
Built-In Self-TestOn-die logic that tests a block without external equipment.
BSDL
Boundary Scan Description LanguageThe machine-readable description of a part's boundary-scan behavior, delivered to board makers.
DFT
Design For TestStructure added to the design purely so it can be tested and debugged — scan, BIST, compression, trace.
DUT
Device Under TestWhatever is currently being tested — a block in simulation or a packaged part on a tester.
DV
Design VerificationProving the RTL does what the specification says, before any silicon exists.
FPGA
Field-Programmable Gate ArrayReconfigurable hardware used to prototype the design far faster than simulation.
ICL
Instrument Connectivity LanguageDescribes how on-die instruments are wired to the IJTAG network.
IJTAG
Internal JTAG (IEEE 1687)A standard for reaching instruments inside the chip through the JTAG port.
JTAG
Joint Test Action Group (IEEE 1149.1)The standard serial access port used for boundary scan, debug and configuration.
MBIST
Memory Built-In Self-TestBIST for embedded memories — the only practical way to test thousands of SRAM instances.
OCC
On-Chip Clock ControllerGenerates the fast clock pulses needed for at-speed scan testing.
PDL
Procedural Description LanguageDescribes how to operate those instruments, alongside ICL.
SDF
Standard Delay FormatBack-annotated delays from the physical design, used to make gate-level simulation realistic.
STIL
Standard Test Interface LanguageA vendor-neutral test pattern format. Translated to tester-native format before use.
TAP
Test Access PortThe JTAG interface pins and controller.
UVM
Universal Verification MethodologyThe standard SystemVerilog framework for building constrained-random testbenches.
VIP
Verification IPA bought testbench component that models a protocol — PCIe, CXL, HBM — so the design can be checked against it.
WGL
Waveform Generation LanguageAn older pattern interchange format, still used by some testers.

Signal, power and package 15

BERT
Bit Error Rate TesterInstrument that drives a high-speed link and counts errors — how link margin is actually measured.
CSAM
C-mode Scanning Acoustic MicroscopyUltrasonic imaging that finds voids and delamination inside a sealed package without destroying it.
EM/IR
Electromigration and IR dropThe two current-related checks on the on-die power grid, usually run as one analysis.
EVB
Evaluation BoardThe lab platform built to bring up and characterize the silicon. Its capability bounds what can be measured.
PCB
Printed Circuit BoardThe board the packaged part is mounted on.
PI
Power IntegrityWhether the supply stays inside its window under real switching current.
PTV
Package Test VehicleThe vehicle program that de-risks assembly and package construction before product silicon commits.
RTD
Resistance Temperature DetectorA resistive on-die or in-package temperature sensor. Needs calibration before its reading is an absolute temperature rather than a relative one.
Rja
Thermal resistance, junction to ambientThe same, measured to the surrounding air — so it includes the cooling solution.
Rjc
Thermal resistance, junction to caseHow many degrees the die rises per watt, measured to the package case. The package's share of the thermal path.
SI
Signal IntegrityWhether a high-speed signal still resembles itself at the far end — loss, reflection, crosstalk, jitter.
SI/PI
Signal and Power IntegrityThe two treated together, because on a high-speed interface they interact.
SIPI
Signal Integrity / Power IntegrityThe stage that owns electrical closure across die, package and board together.
TIM
Thermal Interface MaterialThe compound between die and lid or heatsink. Its bond line thickness directly sets how much power the part can dissipate.
VRM
Voltage Regulator ModuleThe board-level regulator supplying the part. Its transient response has to follow the die's current steps.

Test 12

ATE
Automatic Test EquipmentThe production tester. Its capability, pin count and cost per hour shape the whole test strategy.
DPPM
Defective Parts Per MillionThe escape rate the test flow is designed to achieve. Coverage without a DPPM target is an engineering preference, not a commitment.
FP8
8-bit floating pointA low-precision format used for training and inference.
Fmax
Maximum operating frequencyThe highest clock a part sustains at a given voltage and temperature.
INT8
8-bit integerA low-precision numeric format used for inference. Throughput is quoted per format.
MLPerf
MLPerf benchmark suiteThe industry-standard machine-learning benchmark set customers compare parts with.
PPM
Parts Per MillionRate unit; DPPM is its defective-parts form.
STDF
Standard Test Data FormatThe industry format for per-unit test results. The raw material of all yield analysis.
Shmoo
Shmoo plotA pass/fail map across two swept variables, usually voltage against frequency. Shows where the part stops working, and so how much margin it has.
TOPS
Tera-Operations Per SecondThroughput measure for an accelerator — 10¹² operations a second.
TOPS/W
Tera-Operations Per Second per WattEfficiency measure. The metric this product class is actually bought on.
Vmin
Minimum operating voltageThe lowest supply at which a part still works. Its distribution across units is a core characterization result.

Reliability and compliance 15

AEC
Automotive Electronics CouncilThe body defining automotive-grade qualification, stricter than commercial JEDEC.
CDM
Charged Device ModelThe ESD model where the package itself is charged and discharges through a pin. Scales with package size, so it usually binds on a large 2.5D part.
EMC
Electromagnetic CompatibilityRegulatory limits on emitted and tolerated interference. A market-access gate.
ESD
Electrostatic DischargeA static discharge event the part must survive. Classified by model.
FA
Failure AnalysisPhysically finding out why a part failed. Usually destroys the unit, which matters when there are only a handful.
FIT
Failures In TimeFailures per billion device-hours. The unit reliability commitments are written in.
HBM (ESD)
Human Body ModelThe ESD model representing a person touching a pin. Distinct from HBM the memory — context decides which is meant.
HTOL
High Temperature Operating LifeA thousand hours of powered operation at elevated temperature. The core reliability stress, and the longest fixed item before mass production.
HTS
High Temperature StorageUnpowered bake, which exercises diffusion and interface degradation.
JEDEC
Joint Electron Device Engineering CouncilThe body whose standards define memory interfaces and reliability qualification methods.
MSL
Moisture Sensitivity LevelHow long a package may sit in ambient air before it must be baked prior to soldering. A poor level forces handling procedures on every customer line.
REACH
Registration, Evaluation, Authorization and Restriction of ChemicalsThe broader EU chemicals regulation, with the same supplier-declaration burden.
RoHS
Restriction of Hazardous SubstancesEU restriction on certain materials. Needs a declaration from every component supplier.
THB
Temperature Humidity BiasPowered stress in heat and humidity — finds corrosion and moisture-driven failure.
uHAST
unbiased Highly Accelerated Stress TestPressurized heat and humidity without bias. Accelerates moisture ingress into the package.

Interfaces and memory 14

BER
Bit Error RateHow often a link corrupts a bit. The headline quality number for a high-speed interface.
CXL
Compute Express LinkA coherent protocol layered on the PCIe physical layer, used for memory and accelerator attachment.
D2D
Die-to-DieThe link between two dies inside one package.
ECC
Error Correcting CodeRedundancy that detects and repairs memory errors. Untested correction logic is indistinguishable from working correction logic.
GB/s
Gigabytes per secondBandwidth unit used for memory and interface targets.
HBM
High Bandwidth MemoryStacked DRAM placed beside the die on an interposer. Two stacks are assumed here. Also stands for Human Body Model in ESD contexts.
HBM3
High Bandwidth Memory generation 3The HBM generation assumed in this template; 3E is its extended-speed revision.
HBM3E
High Bandwidth Memory 3 ExtendedThe extended-speed revision of HBM3.
PCIe
Peripheral Component Interconnect ExpressThe host interface standard. Compliance is obtained at scheduled plugfests, not on demand.
PSRR
Power Supply Rejection RatioHow well an analog block ignores noise on its supply. Sets how much PDN noise a PHY tolerates.
RX
ReceiverThe receiving end of a serial link, including its equalization and clock recovery.
TX
TransmitterThe driving end of a serial link.
TX/RX
Transmit / ReceiveThe two directions of a serial link.
UCIe
Universal Chiplet Interconnect ExpressThe standard die-to-die interface for chiplet construction.

Data formats and tooling 16

.lib
Liberty timing libraryTiming, power and noise characterization of a cell across corners. Missing corners silently limit signoff.
AI
Artificial IntelligenceThe product's application domain in this template — a training and inference accelerator.
CAD
Computer-Aided Design (methodology team)The group that owns tool flows, scripts and infrastructure rather than the design itself.
CDL
Circuit Description LanguageThe transistor-level netlist used as the reference for LVS.
EDA
Electronic Design AutomationThe design-tool industry and its licences — a real capacity constraint during peak implementation.
GDS
Graphic Data System (GDSII)The layout database format handed to mask making. OASIS is its modern, smaller replacement.
GDSII
Graphic Data System IIThe full name of the GDS layout format handed to mask making.
HPC
High Performance ComputingThe other workload family such parts serve, with different bandwidth and precision needs.
ID
IdentifierThe stable reference used to trace a requirement, activity or deliverable through the program.
LEF
Library Exchange FormatThe abstract physical view of a cell or macro — outline, pins, blockages — used for placement and routing.
LLM
Large Language ModelThe workload class driving the memory bandwidth and capacity targets assumed here.
ML
Machine LearningThe broader workload family the product serves.
OASIS
Open Artwork System Interchange StandardA compact layout format used instead of GDSII for large databases.
ODB
ODB++ board databaseA PCB manufacturing data format.
QRC
Parasitic extraction (Quantus RC)Extracting resistance and capacitance from layout so timing reflects real wires.
RLC
Resistance, Inductance, CapacitanceThe passive network form used for package and board models.

Appendix B

Schedule tensionsSCHED

Every link in this template was authored as an engineering relationship, then checked against the calendar. These 48 pass the first test and fail the second: the source activity starts after the activity that needs it has already closed.

Some are expected — TC-08 and PTV-12 exist precisely to feed results backwards, and chip-package co-design iterates by construction. Others are real: an input the template assumes is available is not, and the receiving activity has to proceed on a provisional version. Both are listed, largest gap first, because only a program manager can tell them apart.
